title: Dedicated Pricing & Tiers (Draft GTM Deck)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Dedicated Tiers + Throughput SLO: Pricing & Packaging (Draft)
Subtitle: Standardizing Dedicated purchases with clear commitments + predictable unit economics
Footer: Internal draft — do not forward

Speaker notes:
- Audience: Sales, Solutions, CS, Deal Desk, Exec staff
- Goal: align on how we talk about Dedicated vs Hosted, what we guarantee, and the default packages we sell


Slide 2 — Why tiers now (customer pain)
What we hear in the field:
- “I need a throughput guarantee in writing.” (procurement + platform teams)
- Confusion: committed capacity vs observed performance (tokens/sec variability)
- Dedicated today feels bespoke → slow quotes, inconsistent margins, hard to staff on-call

What tiers solve:
- Clear entitlements + escalation paths
- Standard hardware “shapes” → faster provisioning + predictable COGS
- Tier-aware routing/overload behavior → fewer firefights during contention

Speaker notes:
- Use 2–3 recent examples: AlphaBank (written SLO), Vidorama (cost-sensitive but wants burst), HyperDoc (redlines on exclusions/remedies)


Slide 3 — Redwood’s point of view
Competitive advantage shifts from model access → serving economics
Dedicated is for customers who need:
- Predictable throughput + isolation
- Control over model/version pinning
- Stronger operational posture (support, reporting, escalation)

Hosted remains best for:
- Fast iteration, spiky/unknown workloads
- Lower operational overhead

Speaker notes:
- Emphasize “same Redwood API + Console experience” across modes; Dedicated is not a separate product experience


Slide 4 — Definition: what we mean by “throughput”
Canonical metric (customer-facing summary):
- Throughput floor: sustained generation throughput measured as tokens/sec at the deployment level
- Reported as: 95th percentile of 5-minute windows over a rolling 24 hours (draft)

What we measure:
- Model output tokens (streaming-safe accounting)
- Scoped to: a Dedicated deployment_id + pinned model/version + region

What we do NOT promise:
- Latency percentile targets in this document (separate SLA discussion)
- Performance for unsupported context lengths / unsupported model variants

Speaker notes:
- Keep it simple in the deck; detailed semantics live in the SLO doc
- We should be consistent on “deployment-level floor” vs “per-route” language


Slide 5 — Dedicated tiers overview
Three tiers (v1):
1) Standard — predictable baseline
2) Plus — higher floor + defined burst
3) Premium — highest floor + stronger failover posture + fastest support response

Key idea:
- Tiers map to shapes and operational entitlements, not custom promises

Speaker notes:
- Reassure: this does NOT remove customization; exceptions go through Deal Desk with explicit tradeoffs


Slide 6 — Tier entitlements (what customers get)
Standard:
- Throughput floor: guaranteed (shape-based) when within supported config
- Burst: best-effort (no written commitment)
- Failover: best-effort within same region
- Support response: standard enterprise support targets

Plus:
- Throughput floor: higher guaranteed floor
- Burst: defined burst allowance (metered), with documented behavior when exhausted
- Failover: prioritized capacity within region (subject to shape availability)
- Support response: faster initial response + named escalation path

Premium:
- Throughput floor: highest guaranteed floor + tighter variance controls
- Burst: larger allowance + optional reserved burst pool (where available)
- Failover: stronger posture (priority restore; optional multi-AZ / spare node policy per region)
- Support response: fastest response + on-call escalation (contracted)

Speaker notes:
- Don’t say “100% guarantee.” Say “guaranteed floor under defined conditions”
- Align vocabulary with CS: “escalation path” + “service credits for sustained misses”


Slide 7 — What’s included vs add-ons
Included in Dedicated (all tiers):
- Dedicated GPU pool isolated to customer deployment
- Redwood Console: usage + throughput reporting
- Pinned model/version support (supported catalog)
- Change controls: scheduled maintenance windows + release notes

Common add-ons:
- Longer metrics retention / advanced audit exports
- Multi-region standby (Premium only, limited availability)
- Private connectivity options (case-by-case)

Speaker notes:
- Keep add-ons list short; we can expand in 1:1 follow-ups


Slide 8 — Comparison: Dedicated vs Hosted (talk track)
Hosted:
- Pricing: usage-based
- Capacity: shared, rate limited
- Best for: experimentation, variable workloads, quick launches
- Guarantees: API uptime/latency targets (per plan), no throughput floor

Dedicated:
- Pricing: monthly commit (shape-based) + optional burst usage
- Capacity: isolated deployment
- Best for: steady workloads, regulated isolation needs, performance predictability
- Guarantees: throughput floor (tier-based) + escalation/credits

Speaker notes:
- Use “Why not just buy more hosted quota?” → Dedicated gives isolation + predictable sustained throughput


Slide 9 — Hardware shapes: why we standardize
Benefits of shapes:
- Faster provisioning, clearer lead times
- Repeatable benchmark profiles
- Less surprise margin erosion

Messaging:
- Customers pick the tier for entitlement, and a shape for scale
- We recommend a starting shape + scale path (upgrade/downgrade)

Speaker notes:
- Avoid listing every GPU SKU in the deck; keep it “shape families” + regions


Slide 10 — Packaging: recommended deal bundles (v1)
Default packages to quote:
- Standard Starter: 1x baseline shape, single region, pinned model, best-effort burst
- Plus Growth: 1x higher shape OR 2x baseline shapes, defined burst allowance, faster support response
- Premium Enterprise: 2x higher shapes (HA posture), larger burst, contracted escalation + quarterly perf reviews

Common expansions:
- Additional deployments per region (separate commits)
- Model migration support / eval suite add-on

Speaker notes:
- Goal is “off-the-shelf” packages for most deals; reduce custom SKU sprawl


Slide 11 — Pricing model: what Sales needs to know (high-level)
Pricing inputs:
- Tier → entitlement + headroom policy
- Shape → GPU COGS + expected utilization
- Region → supply constraints + lead time

Pricing structure:
- Monthly commit per deployment (shape-based)
- Burst charges (if applicable) are metered separately and appear on invoice/usage export

Guardrails:
- Minimum term / prepay expectations for Plus/Premium (TBD by Finance)
- Discount bands by tier (see Deal Desk slide)

Speaker notes:
- Keep numbers out of the general deck until Finance sign-off; use “bands” or appendix for internal-only


Slide 12 — Discounting & Deal Desk triggers (internal)
Standard:
- Self-serve/AE discretion up to X% (placeholder)
- Deal Desk required beyond X% or non-standard terms

Plus:
- Deal Desk required for:
  - any discount beyond Y%
  - non-standard burst allowance
  - non-standard support commitments

Premium:
- Deal Desk required for all Premium quotes
- Legal review required if SLO language is modified

Speaker notes:
- Add explicit triggers for procurement redlines: remedies, exclusions, measurement disputes


Slide 13 — Procurement questions we expect (and answers)
Q: “Is the throughput guarantee in writing?”
- A: Yes for Plus/Premium (Standard is best-effort language unless otherwise specified)

Q: “How do you measure it?”
- A: Deployment-level tokens/sec; defined measurement windows; excludes customer-side throttling + unsupported configs

Q: “What happens if you miss?”
- A: Escalation + root cause summary; service credits for sustained misses per policy (contracted language)

Q: “Can you guarantee my exact prompt mix?”
- A: Guarantee applies to pinned model/version within supported context/batching guidance; we can benchmark your workload for sizing

Speaker notes:
- Don’t get pulled into “per prompt” guarantees; anchor to supported config + deployment-level measurement


Slide 14 — Positioning: how to choose a tier (simple rubric)
Standard:
- Workload: predictable but tolerant; early Dedicated adoption
- Buyer: engineering

Plus:
- Workload: sustained traffic, clear peak periods, wants defined burst
- Buyer: platform/infra + finance involved

Premium:
- Workload: business-critical, compliance/procurement heavy, needs escalations + stronger failover posture
- Buyer: enterprise procurement + exec sponsor

Speaker notes:
- Give Sales a quick “if you hear X, recommend Y”


Slide 15 — Rollout plan (GTM)
Phase 1 (internal preview):
- Enablement: cheat sheet + talk track + quoting tool export
- Pilot: 5–8 Dedicated accounts (mix of startup + enterprise)

Phase 2 (limited GA):
- Default all new Dedicated quotes to tiers
- Contract language templated for Plus/Premium

Phase 3 (broader):
- Console UI shows tier + throughput floor + recent SLO status
- Expand regions/shapes as supply stabilizes

Speaker notes:
- Keep launch gated on: (1) metric correctness (streaming accounting fix), (2) burn-rate alerts tuned, (3) support playbook ready


Slide 16 — Risks & mitigations
Risk: GPU supply constraints by region break “standard package” promises
- Mitigation: region-specific shape availability + lead time disclosures; Premium reserved procurement path

Risk: Tokens/sec variance causes disputes
- Mitigation: pinned model/version requirement; supported context length guidance; benchmark-based sizing

Risk: Burst creates margin leakage
- Mitigation: meter burst separately; cap burst; tier-aware overload protection

Risk: Alert noise overwhelms SRE
- Mitigation: burn-rate alerts + customer-impact thresholds; dashboards with clear attribution

Speaker notes:
- Keep this slide honest; helps build trust internally and with exec reviewers


Slide 17 — Appendix (internal-only): draft SLO language snippet
Draft concept (not final legal language):
- “For Dedicated Plus and Premium deployments, Redwood will provide a throughput floor of at least [X] tokens/sec for the pinned model/version on the selected shape, measured as the 95th percentile of 5-minute windows over a rolling 24-hour period, excluding periods of customer-side throttling, unsupported configuration, and scheduled maintenance.”

Speaker notes:
- Replace bracketed values with shape-based schedule once Finance/Legal sign off


Slide 18 — Open questions (needs decisions)
1) Which tiers get “in writing” SLO by default? (current: Plus/Premium)
2) Measurement window: 24h vs 7d reporting; how to handle warmup + deploy events
3) Burst: do we sell burst as allowance vs on-demand overage? (metering exists; packaging TBD)
4) Premium failover posture: what’s realistic by region with current supply?
5) Discount guardrails: finalize X/Y% and term requirements

Speaker notes:
- Collect decisions from Product (Lauren), SRE (Sean/Rafael), Finance (Laura/Rishi), Sales Ops (Isabelle)


Slide 19 — Call to action
What we need from Sales leadership:
- Confirm tier names + positioning language (no over-promising)
- Agree on default packages for Q2/Q3 quoting

What we need from Finance:
- Sign off on pricing bands + discount guardrails

What we need from SRE/Infra:
- Confirm shapes supported per region + lead time ranges
- Confirm alerting + escalation readiness before broader rollout

Speaker notes:
- End with timeline: “target enablement training by end of month; pilot quotes next week” (adjust as needed)


Notes (working):
- This deck intentionally avoids hard $ numbers in the main flow. Once pricing is finalized, include an internal appendix slide with:
  - list price bands per tier/shape family
  - example quotes for 1-deployment and HA deployment
  - expected burst line item behavior on invoices
- Make sure we align wording with the Dedicated tier cheat sheet and the customer-facing docs PR before circulating widely.
